headline: HDFC Bank delivered mixed guidance outcomes in Q2-FY26: contingent provisions were built as directed (+Rs.1,600 crores), but NIM compressed a further 8 bps rather than stabilizing, advance growth of 12% in FY26 came in below the system rate of ~13.5-13.9%, and cost-to-income improvement remains a forward commitment without confirmed execution. The CD ratio glide path and FY27 above-system growth targets remain live but unresolved.

segments.Whole Bank: Contingent provisions were increased to above 57 bps of loans (guidance: met), but NIM compressed 8 bps due to front-loaded rate cuts on assets — management now guides exit NIM to move up over the next 4-5 quarters as deposit repricing tailwinds play out (guidance: moving). Advance growth of 12% in FY26 fell short of the guided system-rate target (~13.5-13.9%), though management reaffirmed above-system growth ambition for FY27 with caveats on geopolitical uncertainty (guidance: moving). Cost-to-income improvement was described as a medium-to-long-term operating leverage story with no confirmed ratio reduction this quarter (guidance: moving). CD ratio target of 85-90 in the medium term remains pending with no Q2-FY27 data available.

keyThemes: NIM trajectory: deposit repricing tailwind has 4-5 quarters to run; any additional RBI rate cuts would reset the clock and pressure exit NIM guidance
Loan growth execution: FY27 above-system growth commitment is the key credibility test — watch Q1-FY27 disbursals across retail, MSME, and corporate segments for early confirmation
CD ratio management: incremental credit demand in Q2-FY26 pushed LDR higher sequentially; management must balance growth acceleration against the 85-90 medium-term CD ratio target

Contingent provision buffer and capital deployment: CET1 is elevated, contingent provisions are at record levels — capital allocation optionality (buybacks, accelerated growth, M&A) will be a recurring investor focus in FY27
